name: Localized Lichen Myxedematosus with Mixed Features of Different Subtypes
aliases: Localized Lichen Myxedematosus with Overlapping Subtype Characteristics

criteria.description: Presence of localized waxy papules or nodules with mixed morphological features of different LM subtypes
Skin biopsy showing dermal mucin deposition with fibroblast proliferation without systemic involvement
No evidence of systemic involvement such as thyroid dysfunction or paraproteinemia
Clinical or histological features overlapping multiple localized LM subtypes (e.g., papular mucinosis and nodular forms)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met; minor criteria support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic forms of mucinosis and other cutaneous mucinoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized waxy, firm papules or nodules with mixed morphology
searchTerms: firm, waxy bumps or lumps on skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dermal mucin deposition confirmed by histopathology

common.symptomName: Skin thickening and induration at lesion sites
searchTerms: skin thickening and hardening at lesions

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Mild erythema surrounding papules or nodules
Slow progression of lesion size and number over months
searchTerms: slowly growing skin spots over months
gradual increase in lesion size and number

occasional.symptomName: Mild tenderness on palpation of nodules
Limited joint stiffness near affected skin
searchTerms: limited joint movement close to lesions
mild joint tightness near skin changes

rare.symptomName: Mild peripheral neuropathy symptoms in affected areas
searchTerms: numbness or tingling in affected areas
mild nerve symptoms in skin spots

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of skin lesions

searchTerms: dry skin patches with less sweat

laboratory: Absence of monoclonal gammopathy on serum protein electrophoresis
imaging: Ultrasound may show dermal thickening without deeper tissue involvement
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology: dermal mucin deposition with increased fibroblasts and absence of systemic amyloid or fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Localized papular lesions without mixed subtype features
Absence of mucin deposition on biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions beyond localized areas
Development of systemic symptoms such as fatigue or weight loss
Presence of monoclonal gammopathy or abnormal laboratory findings
references: Rongioletti F, Rebora A. Cutaneous mucinoses: microscopic criteria for diagnosis. Am J Dermatopathol. 2001.
Wollina U. Localized lichen myxedematosus: clinical and histopathological features. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2018.
Orphanet: Localized lichen myxedematosus with mixed features of different subtypes. ORPHA:90398.
